original_card.question: Can a changed G20 helper path or independent-target split improve the complete BIT moment without losing its physical endpoint?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: First read #5679/#5708 and their audits as pending component proposals. Choose one uncovered helper group/cut on an exact word; compare arbitrary-input native action, targets, owned storage, both orientations and full signed bill. Stop if the gain is only a scalar count or repaid by lost targets. Do not rerun the frozen #5609 common-frame domain without changing its hypothesis.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Exact scratch-free unit-ADD minimum of the 18-register chain/exchange component (wires 0-15, 30, 31) of the PR5840 G20 boundary: 20 per side, with both closed 9-wire parts exactly 10. Gates may cross between the parts but stay on the 18 wires.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a changed helper path or independent-target split with a complete BIT moment. This side result instead answers the boundary-synthesis question PR5850 leaves open for the remaining 18-register component, without changing helpers, targets or the recursive profile.
bottleneck_link: Closes one proposed scalar route to a cheaper G20 boundary: joint chain/exchange resynthesis on the component wires cannot beat the source. Remaining scalar routes must use gates leaving the component, scratch, GL2 pair bases or a changed controller.
stop_rule: Stop at the exact minimum for the 18-wire component (or a shorter witness). Do not enlarge to the full 32-wire boundary.
evidence: verify.py: exhaustive budgeted search with admissible row/column bounds, witness replay on all Boolean inputs, four controls; PROOF.md gives the model and a hand proof of the even 9-wire bound.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does any scratch-free ADD word on all 32 boundary wires implement a PR5840 boundary side in fewer than 38 ADDs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This result and PR5850/PR5851 are component-local; gates linking the chain component to the exchange or untouched wires are not covered.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the same budgeted search to the chain component plus one four-wire exchange (22 wires, budget 25) before attempting all 32 wires.
open_questions.blocked_by: Search cost grows quickly with wires and slack; a stronger admissible bound or a written argument is needed.

open_questions.question: Do general GL2 bases inside the equal-target pairs (2k, 2k+1) of the chain component lower its 20-ADD cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Pair bases mix the even and odd 9-wire parts and change the target map, so this exact minimum does not cover them.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the pair-basis orbit of the 18-wire target modulo the bases that leave the cost unchanged and search the cheapest representatives.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each basis change must also be priced at the caller and checked against the target diagonal.
